facts.text: Shinrin-yoku, or forest bathing, means taking in the forest atmosphere; the idea comes from Japan.
Japan's Forestry Agency proposed shinrin-yoku in 1982 as a way to reduce stress.
Forest bathing usually means walking in a forest while consciously using the senses, not hard exercise.
Field studies in Japan linked forest settings with lower cortisol, pulse rate and blood pressure than city settings.
Trees give off airborne oils called phytoncides, which some researchers think may benefit health; the evidence is still limited.
Xitou Nature Education Area in Nantou is part of National Taiwan University's experimental forest.
